properties.name: Design intent is read back into a long build, not only the debt the loop is owed
properties.statement:
A long build session forgets what it was trying to build. reflow's countermeasure was explicit: workflow_master.json takes an architecture_anchor at the P2-to-P3 transition — checksums over the service/functional/interface/graph specs plus captured fields design_intent_summary, key_decisions, constraints, service_count, function_count — and then RE-INJECTS it at three moments: phase_transitions, resync_protocol, and every_N_iterations with N = 5. Its llm_instructions make the purpose plain, on_phase_entry: "Read architecture_anchor from working_memory.json ... Remind yourself of design intent and constraints."

reflow2 HAS a periodic re-injection mechanism and it carries different cargo. cap:read-loop-hint surfaces loop DEBT when it is real — what capture/detect/ask/decide steps are owed — and the Stop hook nudges when graph writes finish without a loop check. That is valuable and is not this. Debt says what you OWE; intent says what you were TRYING TO BUILD. A session can be perfectly clean on debt and still have quietly stopped building the thing the design describes. The vocabulary for the payload largely exists — Snapshot is the checksummed baseline (14 instances against Anchor's zero, see dec:anchor-retire-or-implement), Decision carries key decisions, Constraint carries constraints — so the gap is the RE-READING, not the recording.

THE TRIGGER QUESTION, AMENDED 2026-07-28. This requirement was captured with one thing open: what triggers a re-injection in a system with no phase counter to count iterations against. Reviewing 01-systems_engineering.json answers it, and the answer is two mechanisms rather than one.

(1) A COUNTER. Its context_management block runs an operations counter with threshold 5, tracked in working_memory.json as operations_since_refresh, incremented "after each real operation (file creation, tool execution, artifact generation)" and forcing a refresh at 5. Note the same number as workflow_master's every_N_iterations, so the cadence is consistent across reflow rather than picked twice.

(2) SIGNALS, which is the part with no reflow2 counterpart at all. reflow named the OBSERVABLE SYMPTOMS of context degradation so an agent could notice its own state rather than only counting: "Asking about system name (it's in working_memory.json)", "Forgetting current step", "Working in wrong directory (pwd != system_root)", "Using wrong template format", "Creating artifacts in wrong locations", and "Implementing features not in service_architecture.json" — that last being DRIFT caught behaviourally, from what the agent is about to do, rather than by diffing artifacts after the fact.

The response was a fixed 8-step refresh: PAUSE, VERIFY PWD, SAVE STATE, RELOAD (workflow file, definitions, templates), READ (current focus and progress), CONFIRM (state the system name, workflow, step and next action back), RESET the counter, RESUME. Plus a pre-operation checklist carrying one line worth keeping verbatim: "Verify not about to generate report/summary (do real work)" — an explicit guard against the agent drifting into producing summaries instead of doing the work.

So the trigger is not either/or: a counter bounds how long you can go WITHOUT re-grounding, and signals catch degradation that arrives faster than the counter. A counter alone re-injects on a healthy session and misses a fast collapse; signals alone never fire on the slow drift that has no symptom yet.

STILL OPEN after the amendment: which of reflow's signals survive translation. reflow2 has no pwd, no working_memory.json and no template format, so "wrong directory" and "wrong template" do not port — but "implementing features not in the design", "forgetting what was decided", and "asking for something the graph already holds" all do, and the last is directly observable at the tool boundary. Found 2026-07-28 reviewing the original reflow workflows. Anthony's word: capture it, then amend it.
